sample.data_quality_note: The has_field_data boolean is true for 12617 of 12621 domains (100.0%), but the actual CrUX field metric columns (field_lcp_ms) are only populated for 2887 domains (22.9%). has_field_data appears to default true rather than confirming a real Chrome UX Report match; only field_lcp_ms/field_cls/field_inp_ms being non-null should be treated as 'we have real-user data'.

inp_ms.note: Lighthouse lab INP (inp_ms) is null for every single run in this dataset (0/12621 populated). Lab INP cannot be reported; see field INP below.

page_weight.coverage_note: total-byte-weight is a Lighthouse diagnostic that only appears in the 'items' array when the audit is flagged (i.e. the page payload is large enough to warrant a warning). It is not populated for every domain, so this is a biased sample of heavier-than-ideal sites, not a census of page weight across all domains.

platform_note: 'Custom' is reported at platform_confidence=0.4, meaning no known CMS fingerprint was found -- it is a default/residual label, not a verified bespoke build, and is kept separate from the confidently-fingerprinted CMS platforms (WordPress, Wix, Shopify, Squarespace, Webflow, Framer, all >= 0.7 confidence). 'Unknown' (confidence 0.0) is reported separately again and excluded from any 'platform' narrative claims.

methodology.sample_description: Domains are Australian small/medium businesses gathered by Pryce Digital's own lead scraper (Google Places + ABR sourced), then run once each through Google Lighthouse via the PageSpeed Insights API. This is not a random sample of all Australian websites -- it is skewed toward small local service businesses in the industries we prospect (trades, health, hospitality, professional services, etc), and skewed away from large enterprise or purely e-commerce-at-scale sites.
methodology.strategy: All runs use strategy='mobile' (mobile emulation, throttled network/CPU per Lighthouse defaults). No desktop-strategy top-level rows exist in this table, though a subset of runs carry a secondary desktop score+vitals block in the 'details' JSON, not analysed here.
methodology.single_run_caveat: Each domain has a single Lighthouse run (we take the latest 'ok' run per domain when a domain was re-checked). Individual Lighthouse scores are known to be noisy run-to-run (typically +/- 5-10 performance points) due to lab network/CPU variance; aggregate stats (means, medians, pass rates across thousands of domains) are stable but a single domain's exact score should not be treated as precise.
methodology.platform_detection: Platform is detected heuristically (HTML/header/asset fingerprinting) with a platform_confidence score. We only treat platform_confidence >= 0.7 as a confident CMS match; 'Custom' (0.4) means no fingerprint matched and is not proof of a hand-built site, and 'Unknown' (0.0) means detection failed outright.
methodology.state_derivation: State is derived from a 4-digit postcode found in the free-text Lead.address field using official AU postcode ranges, falling back to a state-abbreviation word match (NSW/VIC/QLD/WA/SA/TAS/NT/ACT) when no postcode is present. Only states with n >= 100 domains are published individually.
methodology.field_data_caveat: The has_field_data boolean is true for 12617 of 12621 domains (100.0%), but the actual CrUX field metric columns (field_lcp_ms) are only populated for 2887 domains (22.9%). has_field_data appears to default true rather than confirming a real Chrome UX Report match; only field_lcp_ms/field_cls/field_inp_ms being non-null should be treated as 'we have real-user data'.

state_by_industry.method: Latest ok mobile-strategy SpeedCheckRun per domain with a non-null performance score (12,621 domains), joined to Lead on the website host (lower-cased, leading www. removed); where several Lead rows share a domain, one with a non-empty address (then a non-empty industry) is preferred. State is derived from the free-text Lead.address: a 4-digit postcode mapped with official AU postcode ranges (the one after a state abbreviation if present, else the last valid one), falling back to a case-insensitive state-abbreviation word match. Industry is the raw Lead.industry label, not the keyword sector groups. A state x industry cell, state total or industry total is published only when n >= 30. Poor = performance < 50; median LCP is lab LCP in seconds. Because of the address-preferring de-duplication, state totals here (3,301 sites with a derivable state) run slightly higher than by_state_min_n100 (3,049).
state_by_industry.result_note: No state x industry cell reaches n >= 30: industry labels are too fine-grained (491 distinct labels across 3,301 state-matched sites, 1,044 cells). The largest cell is VIC Plumber at n = 26.
